clue.text: US singer's big hit? Not right

definitions.note: possessive form; the clue's 's is part of the definition phrase, read as 'the US singer is'

indicators.note: the clue says the big hit is not right, so the letter for right is taken out of it

parts.note: a big hit, a violent collision, is a crash

explanation.surface: A question whether an American singer's chart smash was really any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hit' looks like a chart success, but it is a CRASH; 'Not' removes R (right). The singer is Johnny Cash, the American country star.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny Cash was a celebrated American country singer, so his surname stands for him.

clue.text: Have discussion about problem with a psychologist at last

parts.note: c, for circa, means about
a hitch is a snag or problem

indicators.note: at last picks only the final letter of the word psychologist

explanation.surface: A patient talks about their trouble with a therapist at the end of a session.
explanation.definitionFit: To chitchat is to talk idly, an informal kind of conversation.

clue.text: Trees less healthy on hilly areas, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard spoken aloud, giving sound-alikes

parts.note: less healthy means sicker, and hilly areas are moors; 'on' joins them

explanation.surface: Trees on high ground are reported to be ailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sicker moors' spoken matches the answer; 'on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple common in Britain.

clue.text: Satisfying an itch to pull out during first part of game

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw from a race or contest
during means in

indicators.note: the first part of the word game is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone with an itch is tempted to quit early in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull out' suggests extracting something, but it is withdrawing, as a runner scratched from a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing the skin with the nails relieves an itch; the -ing form matches 'Satisfying'.

clue.text: Daily publicity heralding English pantomime

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British term for a cleaning lady who comes in daily
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A newspaper advert announces an English Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is a CHAR, the British word for a cleaner; 'heralding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a mere pantomime of something.

clue.text: Girl in queue at end of boulevard

indicators.note: at end of places the queue after the street, closing the word

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, a broad street like a boulevard
a queue is a line

explanation.surface: A young woman waits in a line at the far end of a wide street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of boulevard' tempts you to take its last letter, but 'at end of' is only a placing signal, putting the queue after the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Aveline is a female given name of Norman origin.

clue.text: Source of good wine one's located in awfully nice bar in luxury boat

indicators.note: located in means placed inside the reworked letters
awfully means badly, so the letters of the words nice bar are scrambled

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard of high quality wine
one's is I'S, one as I plus 's for is

explanation.surface: A great vintage stands in a dreadful bar aboard a pleasure vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles NICE BAR into CABINER, and 'located in' sets the wine source and one's inside that, just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin cruiser is a motorboat with living quarters, an expensive pleasure craft.

clue.text: Popular charity set up in foreign land

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashion

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means lifted, so the word for charity is read upwards

parts.note: aid is help given as charity

explanation.surface: A well-loved charity is established in an overseas country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia, abroad from the British setter's view.

clue.text: Angry-looking horse upset bird

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns over the whole run of letters so it reads upwards

parts.note: a red face looks angry
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A cross-looking horse frightens a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the horse's mood but turns REDNAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a male goose.

clue.text: Ancient ruler discovered where San Francisco's now located

parts.note: San Francisco is in California, abbreviated CA, so the phrase reads as two words: in, then CA
San Francisco is in California, abbreviated CA, so the phrase reads as two words: in, then CA

explanation.surface: An archaeologist unearths an old king's remains in the Bay Area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now' hints that San Francisco was once Mexican territory; today it lies in CA, the US postal code for California. 'Discovered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sapa Inca was the emperor of the Inca state in pre-Columbian Peru.

clue.text: Bill accommodated by his potty friend, doubling up in German town

indicators.note: doubling up means the piece built so far is written out twice in a row
the bill is taken in, housed inside the friend's name

parts.note: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of children's television, so Bill's friend from the flowerpot is Ben
a bill, an advertisement, is an AD

explanation.surface: Someone shares lodgings with a daft mate and they double up in a German resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben, the Flowerpot Men, were puppets on a 1950s BBC children's show; 'potty' puns on their flowerpots. 'Doubling up' writes the five-letter result twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Baden is a spa town in south-west Germany, in the Black Forest.

clue.text: Bows taken by only some members of the orchestra? Nonsense

definitions.text: Bows taken by only some members of the orchestra
definitions.meaning: the bows used by string players, not the bows performers make to the audience

explanation.definitionFit: Violin bows are what string players use; as an interjection the word means rubbish.

clue.text: Unusual tip to a policeman making tracks

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the following words come out in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A tip-off given to a constable sends someone hurrying away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making tracks' reads as leaving in a hurry, but 'tracks' are recorded songs; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixtape gathers songs chosen from several recordings on one cassette.

clue.text: Shorten a crossing

definitions.meaning: to cut down a text by condensing it
one span carrying a road over a river

explanation.definitionFit: To condense a book is to cut it; read as two words it is one span over water.

clue.text: Exit blocked by riotous sergeants, reeling

indicators.note: reeling means spinning round, so the run taken from the clue words is read backwards
the answer is held in, blocked in by, the run of the words riotous sergeants

explanation.surface: A doorway is jammed by a crowd of drunken, unruly NCOs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters SSERGE sit across the end of 'riotous' and start of 'sergeants'; 'reeling' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal word for a way out or the act of leaving.

clue.text: Among various nations, Switzerland needed support

indicators.note: among puts the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
various means differing, so the letters of nations are shuffled

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Many countries agree Switzerland needs backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' scrambles the letters to STANION, and 'Among' sets Switzerland's code among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar that props something up.

clue.text: Ambassador forged links with one capital city

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, title of an ambassador

indicators.note: forged means made or shaped, so the letters of links are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diplomat built ties with a single capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' looks like 'made' for the ties, but it scrambles LINKS to LSINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

clue.text: Climb a post, say

indicators.note: say indicates that the words are heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a, then to post meaning to send by mail

explanation.surface: Someone is told to climb a pole, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a noun (a pole to climb) but is the verb send; 'a send' spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go up is to rise, the same as climbing.

clue.text: Lover's first caught between two women: a quandary

indicators.note: caught between means held between the two names

parts.note: Di and Emma are two women's names
Di and Emma are two women's names

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word lover

explanation.surface: A man torn between two women faces a tricky choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between alternatives, a real predicament.

clue.text: Copy, I note, is positioned at front of gallery

indicators.note: these words place the earlier pieces ahead of the gallery, so they come first

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a forged painting has been hung at the gallery entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries in London and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic something is to copy it.

clue.text: Trendy lot welcoming new member of royal household

parts.note: trendy means in, fashionable

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for new goes inside

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd greets the newest royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot' looks like a crowd but means one's destiny, FATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An infante is a prince of Spain or Portugal, not heir to the throne.

clue.text: Cake with topping of excellent cream left to cool

indicators.note: topping of picks the first letter of each word in a down clue

parts.note: to air something is to cool it

explanation.surface: A cake with excellent cream on top is left out to cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' suggests cake decoration, but takes the first letters of 'excellent' and 'cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a small cream-filled pastry, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Crimes of villains backing top Italian gangster

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so these pieces follow the earlier ones

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
It is the short form of Italian, as in gin and It
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
fences are criminals who deal in stolen goods

explanation.surface: Mobsters support their Italian godfather in a series of crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a reversal sign but means coming behind. 'It' for Italian vermouth is a British drinks term.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious offences once punishable by death are crimes of the gravest kind.

clue.text: Cooked tripe dish, sort of

definitions.note: the answer is not a dish alone but a kind of dish, as in laboratory work

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so the letters of tripe are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a tripe dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' suggests food, but it is the shallow lab dish used for growing cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is a shallow lab container used for growing bacteria.

clue.text: Extra bit of devotion?

definitions.meaning: an accessory fitted to a machine, or a file added to an email
fond loyalty or affection felt for someone

explanation.definitionFit: An add-on fixed to something is one sense; strong emotional bonding to a person is the other.

clue.text: Favourite accommodation for native of 16

parts.note: F stands for favourite in horse-racing form
an inn provides lodging for travellers

explanation.surface: A best-loved hotel is set aside for a guest from the city at 16.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is HELSINKI, capital of Finland; F for favourite comes from betting on horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a person from Finland, whose capital is the city at 16.

clue.text: Put back in control, say, at end of period

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as on a horse
to say is to state

indicators.note: the end of the word period is just its final letter

explanation.surface: An official is returned to power, it is announced, when a term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' often signals a homophone, but here it is just a synonym; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post is to place them back in it.

clue.text: One in opposition captured by militant insurgents

indicators.note: captured by means the answer is held inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dissenter is taken prisoner by armed rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone opposed to a policy or proposal.
